views.name: orders_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- canonical datetime parsing: keep as TEXT but coalesce empty strings to NULL
  CASE WHEN trim(order_purchase_timestamp) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_approved_at) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_carrier_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_customer_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_estimated_delivery_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM olist_orders

params.description: Order-level canonicalized facts: one row per order with key timestamps and status.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve order-level attributes (status and all primary order timestamps) for reporting or joins. | Filter or slice orders by purchase/approval/delivery/estimated dates. | Serve as the base (grain = order_id) for composing order-level metrics or joining to order-line, payment, review, or customer/seller location data — provided cardinality is handled correctly.
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier of the order (derived directly from olist_orders.order_id) | customer_id: identifier of the customer who placed the order (derived directly from olist_orders.customer_id) | order_status: current status of the order as recorded (derived directly from olist_orders.order_status) | order_purchase_timestamp: order purchase timestamp as text; empty-string values normalized to NULL (derived from olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp after CASE WHEN trim(...) = '' THEN NULL ELSE ... END) | order_approved_at: order approval timestamp as text; empty-string values normalized to NULL (derived from olist_orders.order_approved_at after CASE WHEN trim(...) = '' THEN NULL ELSE ... END) | order_delivered_carrier_date: date/time when carrier accepted the order as text; empty-string values normalized to NULL (derived from olist_orders.order_delivered_carrier_date after CASE WHEN trim(...) = '' THEN NULL ELSE ... END) | order_delivered_customer_date: date/time when customer received the order as text; empty-string values normalized to NULL (derived from olist_orders.order_delivered_customer_date after CASE WHEN trim(...) = '' THEN NULL ELSE ... END) | order_estimated_delivery_date: estimated delivery date as text; empty-string values normalized to NULL (derived from olist_orders.order_estimated_delivery_date after CASE WHEN trim(...) = '' THEN NULL ELSE ... END)
params.grounded_columns: olist_orders.order_id | olist_orders.customer_id | olist_orders.order_status | olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp | olist_orders.order_approved_at | olist_orders.order_delivered_carrier_date | olist_orders.order_delivered_customer_date | olist_orders.order_estimated_delivery_date
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All outputs are base columns (possibly normalized); no SUM/COUNT/AVG/etc. are produced here.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_location on customer_id — safe because orders_base is one-row-per-order and customer_location is expected to be one-row-per-customer (join key = customer_id). This will not duplicate order-level rows provided customer_location is truly one-to-one by customer_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to payments_agg_per_order on order_id — safe because payments_agg_per_order is an aggregate per order (one-row-per-order) so joining on order_id does not multiply order rows and preserves correct order-level aggregation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_revenue_joined on order_id — safe when orders_revenue_joined is known to be a one-row-per-order aggregated revenue view; it will not duplicate order measures. | DO NOT directly join orders_base to order_items_base or order_items_with_product on order_id without re-aggregation, because order_items_* is a one-to-many relation (multiple items per order). Doing a direct join will multiply order-level rows and duplicate any order-level measures. Instead, either: |   - aggregate order_items_* to one row per order (for example SUM(quantity), SUM(price), COUNT(*) per order_id) before joining, or |   - join orders_base -> order_items_* only when the downstream logic expects item-level rows (i.e., when changing the result grain to item-level) and not when preserving order-level measures. | DO NOT directly join to order_reviews_expanded on order_id if that view is one-to-many (multiple reviews per order) without first reducing reviews to order-level (e.g., AVG(review_score) per order) or accepting the change in grain. | When composing further metrics that aggregate orders_base rows (for example COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) or count of orders by date), aggregate on the order_id key from this view. Because this view is normalized to one row per order_id, COUNT(*) on this view equals count of orders in the underlying table after any applied filters.

views.description: Normalized orders table: one row per order with parsed timestamps and canonical status. Use as the cleaned orders dimension for joins and time-based analyses. | Use for: Time-to-delivery calculations per order; Order funnel (purchase -> approved -> delivered) analyses; Filtering orders by status or purchase date range

views.name: order_items_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  shipping_limit_date,
  price,
  freight_value
FROM olist_order_items

params.description: Provides one row per order item with identifiers, seller/product, shipping deadline and monetary amounts (price and freight) for that order item.
params.when_to_use: Get line-level order item details (price, freight) for analytics or joins. | Compute order-level aggregates by re-aggregating these item-level measures (e.g., order total price, total freight) grouped by order_id. | Join to product, seller, or order-level dimensions when those joins are one-to-one (do not multiply item rows) or when downstream logic will re-aggregate after a many join. | Serve as the base for item-level metrics (average item price, count of items per order, item-level revenue analyses).
params.output_schema: order_id: identifier of the order containing this item — derived from olist_order_items.order_id | order_item_id: identifier of the item within the order (line id) — derived from olist_order_items.order_item_id | product_id: identifier of the product for this order item — derived from olist_order_items.product_id | seller_id: identifier of the seller for this order item — derived from olist_order_items.seller_id | shipping_limit_date: the shipping limit / deadline timestamp for this item — derived from olist_order_items.shipping_limit_date | price: the item price paid for this order item (monetary) — derived from olist_order_items.price | freight_value: the freight/shipping cost charged for this order item (monetary) — derived from olist_order_items.freight_value
params.grounded_columns: olist_order_items.order_id | olist_order_items.order_item_id | olist_order_items.product_id | olist_order_items.seller_id | olist_order_items.shipping_limit_date | olist_order_items.price | olist_order_items.freight_value
params.metric: price = base column (olist_order_items.price) — atomic item-level monetary value, not aggregated in this view | freight_value = base column (olist_order_items.freight_value) — atomic item-level monetary value, not aggregated in this view | order_item_count_per_order = COUNT(order_item_id) when aggregated by order_id (example derived metric: must be computed by grouping this view by order_id) | order_total_price = SUM(price) when aggregated by order_id (example derived metric: must be computed by grouping this view by order_id) | order_total_freight = SUM(freight_value) when aggregated by order_id (example derived metric: must be computed by grouping this view by order_id)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on order_id — safe because orders_base is one-row-per-order, so joining orders_base -> order_items_base will expand the order row into its items (this view is already one-row-per-item), and measures in this view remain at item granularity (no duplication of item rows occurs). If you want order-level measures after the join, aggregate order_items_base (e.g., SUM(price) GROUP BY order_id) — do not expect automatic de-duplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_items_with_product on (order_id, order_item_id) — safe when that sibling view preserves the same grain (one-row-per-order_item) because keys match exactly; measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller_location on seller_id only if seller_location is one-row-per-seller (dimension) — safe because each order_items_base row maps to exactly one seller row; item-level measures remain unique per item. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product_size_volume or product dimension on product_id only if that view/table is one-row-per-product (dimension) — safe because each item maps to one product row; preserves item-level cardinality. | do NOT join without re-aggregation: do not join directly to payments_agg_per_order (order-level aggregated payments) on order_id if you expect to preserve item-level sums — joining item-level rows to order-level aggregated rows will replicate the payments row across each item of the order and will therefore multiply item-level rows when computing combined aggregates. If you need combined order-level metrics (payments vs sum of items), first aggregate this view to order_id (e.g., SUM(price), SUM(freight_value)) then join to payments_agg_per_order on order_id. | do NOT join without re-aggregation: do not join to order_reviews_expanded or any reviews table that is one-to-many to orders (multiple reviews per order or per customer) without aggregating reviews first, because that will multiply item rows and overcount item measures. Instead aggregate reviews to the same grain you need (order or customer) before joining. | do NOT join without re-aggregation: do not join to customer_location on customer_id directly from this view, because order_items_base does not contain customer_id — you must join via orders_base (one-row-per-order) to bring in customer_id and then ensure the join to customer_location is one-to-one (dimension) or re-aggregate appropriately. | general rule: this view is strictly at the order-item grain (order_id, order_item_id). When composing, either (a) join only to dimension/lookup tables that are one-row-per-key (product, seller, product dimension views) which will not duplicate item rows, or (b) if joining to any one-to-many aggregated view (order-level aggregates, multiple reviews, multiple payments), first aggregate the side(s) so both sides share a compatible grain before joining to avoid measure multiplication.

views.description: Cleaned order items at the item grain: one row per order item preserving pricing and seller/product linkage. Use for revenue, item-level joins, and SKU/seller performance. | Use for: Revenue or freight aggregation at order/item level; Seller or product contribution to orders; Shipping SLA analysis using shipping_limit_date

views.name: payments_agg_per_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_lines_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total,
  AVG(payment_installments) AS payment_installments_avg,
  -- dominant payment type by summed value per order using a deterministic tie-breaker (min payment_type)
  (SELECT payment_type
   FROM (
     SELECT payment_type, SUM(payment_value) AS v
     FROM olist_order_payments p2
     WHERE p2.order_id = p1.order_id
     GROUP BY payment_type
     ORDER BY v DESC, payment_type ASC
   ) LIMIT 1) AS payment_type
FROM olist_order_payments p1
GROUP BY order_id

params.description: Per-order aggregate of payment lines: counts, sums, average installments and the dominant payment type by value (deterministic tie-breaker).
params.when_to_use: Get payment-level summary metrics per order (e.g., total paid, number of payment lines, avg installments) for analytics or reporting at the order grain. | Join per-order payment metrics into order-level analyses (revenue, RFM, churn) without re-aggregating payments. | Use as a base when composing further aggregations by customer/seller/date — aggregate these per-order measures after joining to avoid double-counting. | Determine the most important payment method for an order (by summed payment_value) for segmentation or payment funnel analysis.
params.output_schema: order_id: the order identifier (olist_order_payments.order_id) — grain/key for this view. | payment_lines_count: number of payment lines for the order (COUNT(*) over olist_order_payments rows for that order). | payment_value_total: total payment value for the order (SUM(payment_value) from olist_order_payments for that order). | payment_installments_avg: average number of installments across the payment lines for the order (AVG(payment_installments) from olist_order_payments for that order). | payment_type: dominant payment_type for the order determined by highest summed payment_value per payment_type; ties broken deterministically by the smallest payment_type (string) — derived from olist_order_payments aggregated per order and per payment_type.
params.metric: payment_lines_count = COUNT(*) over rows in olist_order_payments grouped by order_id | payment_value_total = SUM(olist_order_payments.payment_value) grouped by order_id | payment_installments_avg = AVG(olist_order_payments.payment_installments) grouped by order_id | payment_type = argmax(payment_type) by SUM(olist_order_payments.payment_value) per order_id with deterministic tie-breaker (min payment_type)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on order_id — safe because payments_agg_per_order is one-row-per-order (grain = order_id), so joining preserves one row per order and does not duplicate these aggregated measures. | safe to join to orders_revenue_joined on order_id (one-row-per-order) — no duplication of payment aggregates. | safe to left-join to join-views that are one-row-per-order (for example any normalized order-level view) provided they are known to be at order_id grain. | do NOT join directly to order_items_base or order_items_with_product (order_items is typically one-to-many per order) without re-aggregating, because joining a one-row-per-order payments view to a one-to-many order_items table will multiply the payments_agg_per_order measures across each item row and incorrectly inflate sums (re-aggregation or pre-aggregation is required). | do NOT join without care to order_reviews_expanded or seller_location/customer_location if those sibling views are one-to-many with respect to order_id — verify their grain before joining; if they are many-per-order, aggregate them to order-level first. | When composing higher-level aggregations (e.g., customer-level totals), first join payments_agg_per_order to orders (or to a one-row-per-order view) then aggregate by customer_id. This preserves correctness because payments_agg_per_order is already at order granularity and will not be double-counted when aggregated after a one-to-one join. | If you need payment-level detail (each payment row) instead of per-order aggregates, query olist_order_payments directly; this view cannot be safely exploded back into multiple payment lines.

views.description: Aggregated payment measures per order: total payment value, number of payment attempts, and dominant payment_type inferred by highest total value. Useful for order-level revenue and payment-method analyses. | Use for: Order revenue validation and reconciliation; Payment method mix and counts per order; Correlation of payment attempts with returns or delays

views.name: order_reviews_expanded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.review_id,
  r.order_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_status
FROM olist_order_reviews r
LEFT JOIN olist_orders o
  ON r.order_id = o.order_id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-review joined with the corresponding order metadata (customer, purchase timestamp, order_status), enabling analysis of reviews alongside order context.
params.when_to_use: Count or list reviews and their scores/comments with order-level attributes (customer_id, purchase time, order_status). | Analyze distribution of review_score by order_status, customer segments, or purchase time windows. | Compose with aggregated order-level metrics (revenue, items, payments) while preserving one-row-per-review grain.
params.output_schema: review_id: Unique identifier for the review — derives from olist_order_reviews.review_id | order_id: Order identifier associated with the review — derives from olist_order_reviews.order_id (same key used to join orders) | review_score: Numerical score (rating) of the review — derives from olist_order_reviews.review_score | review_comment_title: Short title or headline of the review comment — derives from olist_order_reviews.review_comment_title | review_comment_message: Full text of the review comment — derives from olist_order_reviews.review_comment_message | review_creation_date: Date when the review was created — derives from olist_order_reviews.review_creation_date | review_answer_timestamp: Timestamp when the seller answered the review (if present) — derives from olist_order_reviews.review_answer_timestamp | customer_id: Identifier of the customer who placed the order related to this review — derives from olist_orders.customer_id | order_purchase_timestamp: Timestamp when the order was purchased — derives from olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_status: Final/current status of the order (e.g., delivered, canceled) — derives from olist_orders.order_status
params.grounded_columns: olist_order_reviews.review_id | olist_order_reviews.order_id | olist_order_reviews.review_score | olist_order_reviews.review_comment_title | olist_order_reviews.review_comment_message | olist_order_reviews.review_creation_date | olist_order_reviews.review_answer_timestamp | olist_orders.customer_id | olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp | olist_orders.order_status
params.metric: review_count = COUNT(review_id)  -- aggregate count of reviews when grouped; review_id is the primary grain column for aggregation | avg_review_score = AVG(review_score)  -- average of review_score over any grouping applied | has_answered = COUNT(review_answer_timestamp) FILTER (WHERE review_answer_timestamp IS NOT NULL)  -- counts reviews that have an answer | reviews_per_order = COUNT(review_id) GROUP BY order_id  -- at this view's grain this will be 1 for orders that have a single review row, but may be >1 if source data contains multiple reviews per order
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base (or other order-level one-row-per-order views) on order_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-review; joining to a one-row-per-order view will not duplicate review rows (the relation is many reviews -> one order). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_location on customer_id — safe if customer_location is one-row-per-customer (one customer row per customer_id). This will not duplicate review rows because review->customer is many-to-one. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_revenue_joined on order_id — safe only if orders_revenue_joined is one-row-per-order (one-to-one with orders). It attaches order-level revenue metrics without duplicating reviews. | do NOT join directly to order_items_base or order_items_with_product (one-to-many: order -> order_items) without re-aggregation first, because each order may have multiple items and joining them will multiply the review rows and thus duplicate any aggregated measures derived from reviews. | do NOT join directly to product_size_volume or any product-level one-to-many tables aggregated per order_item without pre-aggregation to order level, because those joins will also multiply review rows. | When composing with AGG sibling views (e.g., payments_agg_per_order, product_size_volume) prefer joining on order_id to their pre-aggregated-per-order results — safe because the aggregation has collapsed one-to-many relationships to one-row-per-order, avoiding duplication. | If you need item-level detail together with reviews, first aggregate item-level metrics to order_id (e.g., SUM(item_value) GROUP BY order_id) and then join that aggregated result to this view on order_id to keep measures correct.

views.description: Order reviews joined to orders and customers: one row per review including order timestamps and customer identifiers for customer-level sentiment analysis. | Use for: Customer satisfaction and review trends over time; Linking reviews to order timing and status; Per-customer review frequency and scores

views.name: order_items_with_product
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.order_id,
  i.order_item_id,
  i.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  i.seller_id,
  i.price,
  i.freight_value,
  i.shipping_limit_date
FROM olist_order_items i
LEFT JOIN olist_products p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name

params.description: Provides one-row-per-order-item enriched with product attributes and translated product category, for item-level analysis of orders, prices, freight and product characteristics.
params.when_to_use: Compute item-level revenue, freight or price analyses (e.g., average price per item, total freight by item-level filters). | Join product attributes (dimensions like category, size, weight, photos count) to order items for segmentation or filtering before aggregation. | Compose higher-level aggregations (order-level, seller-level, product-level) by aggregating this view up from its order_item grain. | Filter or slice order items by product metadata (category, weight, dimensions) prior to downstream aggregation or modeling.
params.output_schema: order_id: identifier of the order that contains the item — derived from olist_order_items.order_id | order_item_id: identifier of the item line within the order — derived from olist_order_items.order_item_id | product_id: product identifier for the item — derived from olist_order_items.product_id | product_category_name: original product category name (may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_category_name | product_category_name_english: translated English category name (may be NULL) — derived from product_category_name_translation.product_category_name_english | product_name_lenght: length of the product name (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_name_lenght | product_description_lenght: length of the product description (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_description_lenght | product_photos_qty: number of product photos (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_photos_qty | product_weight_g: product weight in grams (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_weight_g | product_length_cm: product length in cm (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_length_cm | product_height_cm: product height in cm (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_height_cm | product_width_cm: product width in cm (numeric, may be NULL) — derived from olist_products.product_width_cm | seller_id: identifier of the seller who sold this item — derived from olist_order_items.seller_id | price: item price charged to the customer for this item (numeric) — derived from olist_order_items.price | freight_value: shipping cost charged for this item (numeric) — derived from olist_order_items.freight_value | shipping_limit_date: deadline date for shipping this item — derived from olist_order_items.shipping_limit_date
params.grounded_columns: olist_order_items.order_id | olist_order_items.order_item_id | olist_order_items.product_id | olist_order_items.seller_id | olist_order_items.price | olist_order_items.freight_value | olist_order_items.shipping_limit_date | olist_products.product_id | olist_products.product_category_name | olist_products.product_name_lenght | olist_products.product_description_lenght | olist_products.product_photos_qty | olist_products.product_weight_g | olist_products.product_length_cm | olist_products.product_height_cm | olist_products.product_width_cm | product_category_name_translation.product_category_name | product_category_name_translation.product_category_name_english
params.metric: price = olist_order_items.price  -- atomic monetary measure stored at order_item grain | freight_value = olist_order_items.freight_value  -- atomic monetary measure stored at order_item grain | item_count = 1 per row  -- implicit count when aggregating rows at this view's grain | aggregated_order_revenue = SUM(price) GROUP BY order_id  -- example aggregation to roll up to order-level | aggregated_order_freight = SUM(freight_value) GROUP BY order_id  -- example aggregation to roll up to order-level
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base on order_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-order_item; joining to orders_base (one-row-per-order) will not duplicate order-item rows when enriching item rows with order-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to seller_location on seller_id — safe because seller_location is expected to be one-row-per-seller (dimension). Enriching items with seller attributes will not duplicate item rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_location only after joining orders_base on order_id (or joining on order->customer mapping) — do NOT join customer_location directly on customer_id unless you first bring customer_id into this view; direct joins from this view to customer-level tables require a deterministic one-to-one key (e.g., order -> customer) to avoid duplication. | do NOT join without care to payments_agg_per_order or product_size_volume (both are AGG views) directly on non-aggregated keys: payments_agg_per_order is one-row-per-order (order-level); you may join it to this view on order_id only if you accept that payments_agg_per_order attributes will be duplicated for each order_item (which is usually intended when enriching items with order-level aggregates). If you want order-level sums without duplication when further aggregating, first aggregate order_items_with_product to order-level (SUM price, SUM freight_value) then join to payments_agg_per_order on order_id. | do NOT join to sibling one-to-many views (for example, order_reviews_expanded) without re-aggregation: joining this item-level view to a reviews view that is one-to-many to orders or items will multiply item-level measures. To preserve correct totals, either (a) aggregate reviews to the same grain before joining, or (b) aggregate this view after the join and use appropriate DISTINCT/conditional expressions. | safe composition pattern: to get seller-level totals, aggregate this view by seller_id (SUM(price), SUM(freight_value), COUNT(1)) and then join to seller_location on seller_id — this prevents duplication caused by joining seller_location first if seller_location were multi-row (it is expected one-row-per-seller). | safe composition pattern: to get order-level metrics combining payments_agg_per_order, first aggregate this view to order_id (SUM price, SUM freight_value, COUNT(1)) and then join to payments_agg_per_order on order_id to combine order-level measures without duplicating sums.

views.description: Order items enriched with product attributes and category name translation. One row per order item with product dimensions for SKU-level analytics and category rollups. | Use for: Category-level revenue and dimensions; Product weight/size impact on freight and delivery; Seller performance within product categories
counter_examples: Identify the top three product categories whose most commonly used payment type has the highest number of payments across all categories, and specify the number of payments made in each category using that payment type.

views.name: seller_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
FROM olist_sellers s
LEFT JOIN olist_geolocation g
  ON s.seller_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_zip_code_prefix, s.seller_city, s.seller_state

params.description: Provides one-row-per-seller canonical location information (zip, city, state) plus the seller's representative latitude/longitude computed as the average of matched geolocation points.
params.when_to_use: Find seller address and representative geographic coordinates for mapping or distance calculations | Enrich seller-level reports (orders by seller, revenue by seller) with seller location attributes | Join seller geographic attributes into downstream analyses that operate at the seller level
params.output_schema: seller_id: Unique identifier of the seller — sourced from olist_sellers.seller_id | seller_zip_code_prefix: Seller postal code prefix (string or numeric as in source) — sourced from olist_sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix | seller_city: Seller city name — sourced from olist_sellers.seller_city | seller_state: Seller state abbreviation — sourced from olist_sellers.seller_state | geolocation_lat: Representative latitude for the seller — computed as AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lat) over geolocation rows matching the seller_zip_code_prefix | geolocation_lng: Representative longitude for the seller — computed as AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lng) over geolocation rows matching the seller_zip_code_prefix
params.grounded_columns: olist_sellers.seller_id | olist_sellers.seller_zip_code_prefix | olist_sellers.seller_city | olist_sellers.seller_state | olist_geolocation.geolocation_lat | olist_geolocation.geolocation_lng | olist_geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
params.metric: geolocation_lat = AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lat)  -- average latitude of geolocation rows matched by zip prefix | geolocation_lng = AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lng)  -- average longitude of geolocation rows matched by zip prefix
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any seller-level table or view on seller_id (for example orders_agg_by_seller or orders_revenue_joined aggregated to seller) — safe because seller_location has one row per seller_id, so joining on seller_id will not duplicate seller_location's aggregate coordinates. | safe to join to seller-dimension-like views: join to views that are explicitly one-row-per-seller (e.g., a normalized sellers_base or another seller-level aggregate) on seller_id — measures in this view are not multiplied because keys are 1:1. | do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables (for example order_items_base, orders_base, payments_agg_per_order, order_reviews_expanded) without first aggregating those tables to seller_id: joining seller_location (1 row per seller) to a raw orders or order_items table (many rows per seller) will produce repeated seller_location rows and therefore duplicate the implicit per-seller coordinate values in downstream aggregations. Instead, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many table to seller_id first (e.g., SUM(order_amount) GROUP BY seller_id) and then join to seller_location on seller_id, or | - perform the join and then re-aggregate at seller_id-level, making clear which measures should be aggregated and how. | zip-code-based caution: this view computes coordinates by averaging geolocation rows matched on seller_zip_code_prefix. If you plan to join merchant-level records using zip_code_prefix rather than seller_id, be aware multiple sellers may share the same zip_code_prefix; joining on zip may produce many-to-one or one-to-many relationships and could duplicate measures—prefer joining on seller_id when composing seller-level metrics. | joins to geospatial or mapping tables are safe when done on seller_id or when the other table is also one-row-per-seller; avoid joining to raw geolocation table (olist_geolocation) directly because it is many-to-one with seller_location and would multiply the averaged coordinates unless you re-aggregate after the join.

views.description: Seller table joined to geolocation centroid per zip prefix: one row per seller with a representative latitude/longitude (avg) for the seller_zip_code_prefix. Useful for mapping and distance calculations. | Use for: Spatial analyses of sellers; Mapping seller distribution by state/city; Distance from seller to customer zip (when customer coords available)

views.name: customer_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
FROM olist_customers c
LEFT JOIN olist_geolocation g
  ON c.customer_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_unique_id, c.customer_zip_code_prefix, c.customer_city, c.customer_state

params.description: Provides one-row-per-customer demographic and average-geolocation (lat/lng) derived from customer ZIP-code-linked geolocation records.
params.when_to_use: Look up customer-level attributes (city, state, ZIP prefix) and a representative latitude/longitude for mapping or spatial joins. | Compose customer-level analyses that need a single geolocation per customer (e.g., customer-level mapping, distance calculations to sellers or warehouses) without re-aggregating geolocation records. | Join to order- or transaction-level aggregates when you need customer attributes attached to each customer key before further aggregation.
params.output_schema: customer_id: unique identifier for the customer (source: olist_customers.customer_id) | customer_unique_id: stable customer identifier for deduplication across orders (source: olist_customers.customer_unique_id) | customer_zip_code_prefix: customer's ZIP code prefix used to link to geolocation (source: olist_customers.customer_zip_code_prefix) | customer_city: city of the customer (source: olist_customers.customer_city) | customer_state: state of the customer (source: olist_customers.customer_state) | geolocation_lat: average latitude of all geolocation records that match the customer's ZIP code prefix (derived metric: AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lat)) | geolocation_lng: average longitude of all geolocation records that match the customer's ZIP code prefix (derived metric: AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lng))
params.grounded_columns: olist_customers.customer_id | olist_customers.customer_unique_id | olist_customers.customer_zip_code_prefix | olist_customers.customer_city | olist_customers.customer_state | olist_geolocation.geolocation_lat | olist_geolocation.geolocation_lng | olist_geolocation.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
params.metric: geolocation_lat = AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lat) grouped at customer_id (aggregation performed after LEFT JOIN on ZIP prefix) | geolocation_lng = AVG(olist_geolocation.geolocation_lng) grouped at customer_id (aggregation performed after LEFT JOIN on ZIP prefix)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base (or any order-level view) on customer_id — safe because this view is one-row-per-customer (customer_id) so joining customer_location -> orders (one-to-many) will expand the customer row per order, but will not duplicate aggregated measures housed in orders; if you need to preserve customer-level measures after joining to many-rows, aggregate the result appropriately. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_order_agg on customer_id — safe because customer_order_agg is already aggregated per customer (one-row-per-customer), so joining two one-row-per-customer objects will not duplicate measures. | do NOT join this view to a one-to-many table/view (for example order_items_base, order_reviews_expanded, order_items_with_product) without considering re-aggregation — joining directly will repeat the customer row for each matching child row and thereby implicitly multiply any metrics that are counts/aggregates if you treat them as already-aggregated. | when joining to seller_location or other location-level JOINs, prefer joining via keys that maintain 1:1 semantics (e.g., if you join customer_location to seller_location via a derived mapping table that yields one seller per customer), otherwise re-aggregate the result to the intended grain to avoid measure duplication. | if you need to compute customer-level metrics that combine this view's geolocation averages with metrics from multi-row child tables, first aggregate the child tables to customer_id (or join this view to a pre-aggregated child view such as payments_agg_per_order aggregated to customer) so composition remains cardinality-safe. | explicit note on JOIN keys: this view is one-row-per olist_customers.customer_id because GROUP BY includes customer_id and other customer attributes; joins on customer_id are the intended safe path for 1:1 merges with other customer-grain datasets.

views.description: Customer table joined to geolocation centroid per zip prefix: one row per customer with representative latitude/longitude (avg) for the customer_zip_code_prefix. Use for customer spatial segmentation and distance-based features. | Use for: Customer geographic segmentation and mapping; Proximity-based marketing and delivery estimations; Aggregating orders by customer region

views.name: orders_revenue_joined
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  COALESCE(item_revenue.total_price, 0.0) AS total_items_price,
  COALESCE(item_revenue.total_freight, 0.0) AS total_freight_value,
  p.payment_lines_count,
  p.payment_value_total
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(price) AS total_price, SUM(freight_value) AS total_freight
  FROM olist_order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) item_revenue
  ON o.order_id = item_revenue.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS payment_lines_count, SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total
  FROM olist_order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) p
  ON o.order_id = p.order_id

params.description: Per-order revenue and payment summary combining order header with aggregated item revenue and payment metrics (one row per order_id).
params.when_to_use: Report total item revenue, freight, and payment totals per order | Filter orders by customer, status, or purchase timestamp while retaining per-order monetary metrics | Use as a building block (safe aggregated input) when composing higher-level aggregations by order_id (e.g., customer-level or period-level revenue) | Join with one-row-per-order dimensions (customer, seller, order review) to enrich orders without duplicating monetary measures
params.output_schema: order_id: unique identifier for the order — from olist_orders.order_id | customer_id: id of the customer who placed the order — from olist_orders.customer_id | order_status: current status of the order (e.g., delivered, canceled) — from olist_orders.order_status | order_purchase_timestamp: timestamp when the order was purchased — from olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp | total_items_price: sum of order item prices for the order (SUM(olist_order_items.price) grouped by order_id; 0.0 if no items) — derived from item_revenue.total_price which aggregates olist_order_items.price | total_freight_value: sum of freight_value for the order (SUM(olist_order_items.freight_value) grouped by order_id; 0.0 if no items) — derived from item_revenue.total_freight which aggregates olist_order_items.freight_value | payment_lines_count: number of payment lines recorded for the order (COUNT(*) on olist_order_payments grouped by order_id; NULL if no payments) — from p.payment_lines_count | payment_value_total: sum of payment_value for the order (SUM(olist_order_payments.payment_value) grouped by order_id; NULL if no payments) — from p.payment_value_total
params.grounded_columns: olist_orders.order_id | olist_orders.customer_id | olist_orders.order_status | olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp | olist_order_items.order_id | olist_order_items.price | olist_order_items.freight_value | olist_order_payments.order_id | olist_order_payments.payment_value
params.metric: total_items_price = COALESCE( SUM(olist_order_items.price) OVER per-order aggregation, 0.0 ) — implemented as SUM(price) grouped by order_id in the item_revenue subquery | total_freight_value = COALESCE( SUM(olist_order_items.freight_value) OVER per-order aggregation, 0.0 ) — implemented as SUM(freight_value) grouped by order_id in the item_revenue subquery | payment_lines_count = COUNT(*) OVER per-order aggregation on olist_order_payments — implemented as COUNT(*) grouped by order_id in the p subquery | payment_value_total = SUM(olist_order_payments.payment_value) OVER per-order aggregation — implemented as SUM(payment_value) grouped by order_id in the p subquery
params.composition: Safe to join to customer-level one-row-per-customer views/tables on orders_revenue_joined.customer_id because this view is one row per order_id; joining will not duplicate order-level measures when keyed by customer_id if downstream aggregation re-aggregates by customer_id (i.e., GROUP BY customer_id) — example safe join: customer_location ON customer_id | Safe to join to one-row-per-order sibling views (e.g., orders_base, order_reviews_expanded, orders_rank_by_purchase) on order_id because those are one-row-per-order and will not multiply measures — join on order_id | Do NOT join directly to raw order_items (olist_order_items) or any other one-to-many table (order_items_with_product, product_size_volume if it's per-item) on order_id without re-aggregation first because those are many rows per order and would multiply total_items_price/total_freight_value/payment_value_total. If you need item-level detail, either: | - join and then re-aggregate measures correctly (e.g., SUM(distinct order_id measures) is invalid); or | - instead join to an aggregated-by-order view (like the item_revenue subquery or order_items_base aggregated per order) to preserve cardinality. | Do NOT join to payments_agg_per_order if it produces multiple rows per order or includes additional payment-line detail; if payments_agg_per_order is one-row-per-order (aggregated), it is safe to join on order_id — otherwise aggregate payments by order_id first. | When composing higher-level aggregations (e.g., customer or period totals), treat the monetary columns (total_items_price, total_freight_value, payment_value_total) as already-aggregated measures at the order grain and SUM them after joining/filtering. Do not SUM raw joins against child tables without first collapsing them to order_id to avoid double-counting. | If joining to dimensions keyed at a different grain (e.g., product or seller which are many-per-order), either aggregate those dimensions to one row per order before joining or perform joins that do not multiply rows (e.g., use EXISTS/IN or lateral subqueries that select single aggregated values).

views.description: Order-level revenue and payment summary joined to order metadata: one row per order with total item revenue, total freight, and payment aggregates. Use for order profitability and revenue analysis. | Use for: Order-level revenue vs payments reconciliation; Identifying orders with missing payment/price records; Profitability and freight cost analysis per order

views.name: product_size_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_name_lenght,
  product_description_lenght,
  product_photos_qty,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm,
  -- compute cubic volume in cubic centimeters when dims available
  (product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm) AS product_volume_cm3,
  -- simple size flag: 1 if any dimension or weight present (demonstrative derived column)
  CASE WHEN (product_weight_g IS NOT NULL OR product_length_cm IS NOT NULL OR product_height_cm IS NOT NULL OR product_width_cm IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_size_info
FROM olist_products

params.description: Per-product size and basic descriptive attributes (one row per product) including computed cubic volume and a simple size-availability flag.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve product physical attributes (weight, dimensions) and simple derived volume for reporting or enrichment. | Filter or segment products by having any size information (has_size_info) or by numeric thresholds on weight/dimensions/volume. | Join product-level size attributes into order-, item-, seller- or customer-level analyses while preserving correct cardinality when done as a 1:many enrichment. | Serve as a building block when computing product-level aggregates before joining to order-item-level data (must avoid duplicating measures).
params.output_schema: product_id: unique product identifier at product grain — sourced from olist_products.product_id | product_category_name: product category name — sourced from olist_products.product_category_name | product_name_lenght: length of product name (precomputed) — sourced from olist_products.product_name_lenght | product_description_lenght: length of product description (precomputed) — sourced from olist_products.product_description_lenght | product_photos_qty: number of product photos (precomputed) — sourced from olist_products.product_photos_qty | product_weight_g: product weight in grams — sourced from olist_products.product_weight_g | product_length_cm: product length in centimeters — sourced from olist_products.product_length_cm | product_height_cm: product height in centimeters — sourced from olist_products.product_height_cm | product_width_cm: product width in centimeters — sourced from olist_products.product_width_cm | product_volume_cm3: computed cubic volume in cubic centimeters (product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm) — derived from product_length_cm, product_height_cm, product_width_cm | has_size_info: binary flag (1/0) indicating presence of any of product_weight_g, product_length_cm, product_height_cm, or product_width_cm — derived from those base columns
params.grounded_columns: olist_products.product_id | olist_products.product_category_name | olist_products.product_name_lenght | olist_products.product_description_lenght | olist_products.product_photos_qty | olist_products.product_weight_g | olist_products.product_length_cm | olist_products.product_height_cm | olist_products.product_width_cm
params.metric: product_volume_cm3 = product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm (row-level arithmetic; NULL if any operand is NULL) | has_size_info = CASE WHEN (product_weight_g IS NOT NULL OR product_length_cm IS NOT NULL OR product_height_cm IS NOT NULL OR product_width_cm IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END (row-level boolean indicator)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_items_with_product on product_id — safe when order_items_with_product is used only to bring product attributes onto items if you do NOT aggregate order_items_with_product first, because product_size_volume is one-row-per-product; however joining this AGG directly to a many-row order_items relation will replicate product rows across each matching order_item row (this is expected for enrichment, but if you want to preserve product-level measures you should aggregate after the join). | Safe to join to seller_location or customer_location via their keys only when those joins are 1:1 to the product grain (they are typically 1:many relative to orders/customers, so ensure you join product_size_volume to seller or customer only through an intermediate 1:1 relationship, e.g., product->seller if such mapping exists). | Do NOT blindly join to orders_base, order_items_base, payments_agg_per_order, order_reviews_expanded, orders_revenue_joined, or customer_order_agg without considering multiplicity: these are many-to-one or one-to-many relative to product_id and will duplicate product-level derived measures if you need product-level uniqueness. If you need product-level metrics after joining to a many-row table, either (a) aggregate the joined result back to product_id (e.g., SUM/AVG over desired measures) or (b) join product_size_volume after performing necessary aggregations on the many-side to a single row per product_id. | General rule for planners: product_size_volume is one-row-per product_id (grain = product_id). Any join on product_id to a table that is also one-row-per-product_id will preserve measure correctness; joins to tables with multiple rows per product_id will multiply product rows and therefore must be followed by re-aggregation or used only for enrichment of each matching row (not for computing product-level aggregates).

views.description: Per-product physical volume and derived size metrics: one row per product with computed cubic volume and a simple size indicator. Useful for logistics and shipping impact analyses. | Use for: Estimating shipping costs from product volume/weight; Filtering SKUs by available dimension metadata; Category-level average size/weight

views.name: orders_rank_by_purchase
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_status,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS customer_order_rank
FROM olist_orders

params.description: Provides each order with its rank (most-recent = 1) within the ordering history of its customer.
params.when_to_use: Ask for the position of an order in a customer's purchase history (e.g., identify first order, repeat orders, Nth most recent order). | Filter or segment orders by recency per customer (e.g., only keep customers' latest order, top-N recent orders). | Compose customer-level features that depend on order ordering (e.g., time-between-orders for order #k) by joining to this ranked ordering and then aggregating. | Join to order-level details while preserving per-order rank information for analytics or machine learning features.
params.output_schema: order_id: the unique identifier of the order — derived from olist_orders.order_id | customer_id: the identifier of the customer who placed the order — derived from olist_orders.customer_id | order_purchase_timestamp: timestamp when the order was purchased — derived from olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp | order_status: order lifecycle status at the order level (e.g., delivered, shipped) — derived from olist_orders.order_status | customer_order_rank: RANK() over orders for the same customer ordered by order_purchase_timestamp DESC (1 = most recent). This is a window-derived ordinal (ties receive same rank) computed from olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp partitioned by olist_orders.customer_id
params.metric: customer_order_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY olist_orders.customer_id ORDER BY olist_orders.order_purchase_timestamp DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_base (or any dimension/view that is strictly one-row-per-order) on order_id — safe because orders_rank_by_purchase is exactly one row per order_id (grain = ['order_id']), so measures/row counts are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to payments_agg_per_order on order_id — safe because payments_agg_per_order is an aggregation per order (one-row-per-order); joining on order_id will not multiply rows and preserves the rank correctly. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to order_reviews_expanded on order_id only if order_reviews_expanded is known to be one-row-per-order; if order_reviews_expanded is one-to-many (multiple reviews per order) do NOT join directly without re-aggregation because that would duplicate orders and inflate any counts/metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_revenue_joined on order_id — safe if orders_revenue_joined is one-row-per-order (it is named JOIN but ensure it's one-row-per-order); otherwise aggregate revenue to order-level first before joining. | do NOT join directly to order_items_base, order_items_with_product, or product_size_volume without re-aggregating those item-level tables to order-level first (e.g., SUM(quantity), SUM(price), COUNT(items)) because these are one-to-many with respect to orders and would multiply the single row-per-order in this view and thus duplicate the customer_order_rank and any order-level measures. | do NOT join directly to customer_order_agg on customer_id unless you intend to have multiple orders per customer remain as multiple rows here; joining customer-level aggregates (one-row-per-customer) to this one-row-per-order view on customer_id is safe (it will repeat customer aggregates across that customer's orders) — repeating customer-level attributes is expected but does not multiply order rows beyond their correct multiplicity. | when composing larger aggregations: if you aggregate after joining to one-to-many tables, make sure to re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., customer or order) and not assume this view's window-derived rank aggregates correctly across the multiplied rows. Prefer joining only order-level or customer-level aggregates (one-row-per-order or one-row-per-customer) to maintain correctness.

views.description: Rank orders per customer by purchase timestamp (most recent rank 1). One row per order with customer-scoped rank to support top-K queries per customer (e.g., latest N orders). | Use for: Latest orders per customer; Churn detection using recency metrics; Customer lifetime ordering patterns

views.name: customer_order_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(items.total_price,0.0)) AS total_spent,
  AVG(COALESCE(items.total_price,0.0)) AS avg_order_value,
  AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_review_score
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(price) AS total_price
  FROM olist_order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) items
  ON o.order_id = items.order_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_reviews r
  ON o.order_id = r.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id

params.description: Per-customer aggregates of orders, spend and review score — useful for customer-level lifetime and behavior analysis.
params.when_to_use: Get total orders, total spent, average order value, and average review score per customer. | Segment customers by spend or order count for retention/marketing use cases. | Compose customer-level features for modelling (RFM-like features) by joining customer dimension safely. | Aggregate further (e.g., by region or cohort) by grouping these per-customer metrics.
params.output_schema: customer_id: unique identifier for the customer — derived from olist_orders.customer_id | orders_count: number of distinct orders placed by the customer — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT olist_orders.order_id) | total_spent: sum of per-order total prices for this customer's orders — derived from SUM(COALESCE(items.total_price,0.0)) where items.total_price is SUM(price) from olist_order_items per order | avg_order_value: average of per-order total prices for the customer's orders — derived from AVG(COALESCE(items.total_price,0.0)) where items.total_price is SUM(price) from olist_order_items per order | avg_review_score: average review_score across that customer's orders (NULL if no reviews) — derived from AVG(olist_order_reviews.review_score)
params.grounded_columns: olist_orders.customer_id | olist_orders.order_id | olist_order_items.order_id | olist_order_items.price | olist_order_reviews.order_id | olist_order_reviews.review_score
params.metric: orders_count = COUNT(DISTINCT olist_orders.order_id) | total_spent = SUM(COALESCE(items.total_price, 0.0))  where items.total_price = SUM(olist_order_items.price) GROUP BY olist_order_items.order_id | avg_order_value = AVG(COALESCE(items.total_price, 0.0))  (average of per-order totals for orders belonging to the customer) | avg_review_score = AVG(olist_order_reviews.review_score)  (average of review_score values for the customer's orders)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer_location on customer_id — safe because this view is one row per customer_id, so joining a one-row-per-customer dimension (customer_location) will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_revenue_joined on customer_id ONLY IF orders_revenue_joined is also aggregated to one row per customer; otherwise re-aggregate orders_revenue_joined to customer-level before joining. Safe when both sides are at customer grain. | DO NOT join directly to olist_order_items (one-to-many: order_items per order) without re-aggregation: joining raw order_items to this per-customer view will multiply orders_count, total_spent and avg_order_value because order_items expand orders into multiple rows. | DO NOT join directly to olist_order_reviews (one-to-many: multiple reviews per order) without re-aggregating reviews to the order- or customer-level first — joining raw reviews can duplicate orders_count and distort averages. | DO NOT join to orders_base or order_reviews_expanded unless those views are reduced to one row per customer (or you re-aggregate after the join). If you need additional order-level attributes, join this customer-level view to an order-level view via customer_id only when the order-level view is first aggregated to customer-level (e.g., SUM or COUNT per customer). | When composing: prefer to (a) join this view to dimensions that are one-row-per-customer, or (b) join at a lower grain (orders) by re-deriving/aggregating measures from base tables. Example safe pattern — to get customer spend by region: join customer_location (one-row-per-customer) to this view on customer_id and then aggregate across region. Unsafe pattern — joining this view to order_items_with_product (order_items-level) will multiply rows and require re-aggregation of metrics.

views.description: Aggregated order-level metrics per customer: counts of orders, total spent (from items), average order value and average review score when available. Useful for customer segmentation and LTV proxies. | Use for: Customer lifetime value estimation; Segmentation by spend and satisfaction; Identifying high-value customers

views.name: orders_delivered_with_purchase_timestamp
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS INTEGER) AS purchase_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS INTEGER) AS purchase_month
FROM orders_base o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: One row per order that was delivered, with canonical parsed purchase timestamp components (year, month) and core order identifiers and status. Useful to build time-based cohorts and monthly/yearly counts for delivered orders.

views.name: orders_purchase_timestamp_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS INTEGER) AS purchase_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS INTEGER) AS purchase_month,
  date(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS purchase_date
FROM
  orders_base o
views.description: Normalized projection of orders with parsed datetime parts extracted from order_purchase_timestamp. Exposes order_id, order_status and canonical integer year and month to support many temporal analyses (filters, group-bys, joins).

views.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value
FROM olist_order_items oi
JOIN olist_products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN olist_sellers s
  ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
views.description: Order items enriched with product and seller identifiers and pricing measures. Exposes order_id, product_id, seller_id, price, freight_value to support revenue/price breakdowns and joins back to orders for temporal aggregation.

views.name: orders_delivered_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_status,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', order_purchase_timestamp) AS INTEGER) AS order_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', order_purchase_timestamp) AS INTEGER) AS order_month,
  customer_id
FROM orders_base
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: One-row-per-order events limited to orders that reached delivered status; exposes purchase timestamp and parsed year/month for time-based grouping and filtering.

views.name: orders_purchase_date_normalized
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  -- canonical timestamp: try to cast to TEXT normalized ISO by parsing known format; keep original if null
  CASE
    WHEN length(o.order_purchase_timestamp) >= 10 THEN substr(o.order_purchase_timestamp,1,19)
    ELSE o.order_purchase_timestamp
  END AS order_purchase_timestamp_canonical,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CASE WHEN length(o.order_purchase_timestamp) >= 10 THEN substr(o.order_purchase_timestamp,1,19) ELSE o.order_purchase_timestamp END) AS INTEGER) AS order_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', CASE WHEN length(o.order_purchase_timestamp) >= 10 THEN substr(o.order_purchase_timestamp,1,19) ELSE o.order_purchase_timestamp END) AS INTEGER) AS order_month
FROM orders_base o
views.description: Normalized order purchase timestamp with explicit parsed integer year and month fields and canonical timestamp cast; keeps one row per order_id from orders table for consistent time parsing.

views.name: orders_with_customer_and_item_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  strftime('%Y', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_year,
  strftime('%m', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS order_month,
  o.order_status,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.price AS item_price,
  oi.freight_value AS item_freight_value
FROM orders_base o
JOIN order_items_base oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
LEFT JOIN customer_location c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
views.description: Denormalized order-level view joining orders to items and customers to expose customer id, seller id(s), item counts and simple monetary measures per order (price, freight) without aggregating across orders. Useful for queries that need per-order counts or sums and linking to customers/sellers.

views.name: delivered_orders_with_customer
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state
FROM olist_orders AS o
JOIN olist_customers AS c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
grain: order_id  -- one row per order (only orders that have a matching customer)
views.description: One row per delivered order joined to its customer. Exposes order identifiers, customer identifiers (both the surrogate customer_id and the reusable customer_unique_id), order timestamps and status so downstream queries can filter, group and join. Excludes orders without a matching customer to support calculations that require customers.

views.name: order_payments_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  payment_sequential,
  payment_type,
  payment_installments,
  payment_value
FROM olist_order_payments
grain: order_id, payment_sequential  -- one row per payment record
views.description: Raw payments table exposing each payment record per order. Keeps all payment rows (multiple sequential payments per order) so callers can compute sums/averages/counts per order or per customer as needed.

views.name: customer_dimension
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  customer_unique_id,
  customer_zip_code_prefix,
  customer_city,
  customer_state
FROM olist_customers
grain: customer_id  -- one row per customer_id (customer_unique_id may repeat across customer_id in dataset but both are exposed)
views.description: Canonical customer dimension exposing stable customer keys and main location attributes. Useful for grouping by customer_unique_id or reporting customer attributes alongside metrics.

views.name: customers_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  customer_unique_id,
  customer_city,
  customer_state,
  customer_zip_code_prefix
FROM olist_customers
views.description: Canonicalized customer rows exposing customer identifiers and location (city/state/zip). Keep one row per customer_id.

views.name: delivered_orders
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM olist_orders AS o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: Orders that reached delivered status, exposing order identifiers, customer link and key timestamps for downstream joins and time-based filters.

views.name: order_payment_items_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.order_id AS order_id,
  p.payment_sequential AS payment_sequential,
  p.payment_type AS payment_type,
  p.payment_installments AS payment_installments,
  p.payment_value AS payment_value,
  o.customer_id AS customer_id,
  c.customer_city AS customer_city,
  c.customer_state AS customer_state
FROM olist_order_payments p
JOIN olist_orders o
  ON p.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
grain: one row per olist_order_payments row (payment for an order) with associated customer and order info
views.description: Denormalized payments per order (one row per payment record) joined with delivered orders and customers so each payment row includes order, customer and customer city/state. Useful to aggregate payments by customer location or by order.

views.name: delivered_orders_23
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_carrier_date,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date,
  o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
  o.order_status
FROM olist_orders o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: All orders that reached customers with status = 'delivered'. Keeps order identifiers and timestamps for joins to items and reviews.

views.name: order_items_with_seller_and_price
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  price,
  freight_value,
  shipping_limit_date
FROM order_items_base
views.description: Order items enriched with seller, price and freight so profits and order-level attributions can be computed. One row per order_item (order_id + order_item_id).

views.name: orders_customers_unique
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN customer_dimension c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
grain: one row per order_id (one-to-one mapping to customer for olist_orders)
views.description: Maps orders to customers and canonical customer_unique_id; useful to count distinct customers per seller via orders.

views.name: order_item_product_category_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id AS order_id,
  oi.product_id AS product_id,
  p.product_category_name AS product_category_name,
  oi.order_item_id AS order_item_id,
  oi.seller_id AS seller_id,
  oi.price AS price,
  oi.freight_value AS freight_value,
  oi.shipping_limit_date AS shipping_limit_date
FROM order_items_base AS oi
JOIN olist_products_dataset AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.product_category_name IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per order_id + order_item_id (i.e., each line item)
views.description: Maps order items to product categories using the product dataset, one row per order-item-product with cleaned category. Useful to attribute orders (and their payments) to product categories. Exposes order_id, product_id and product_category_name for downstream grouping and joins.

views.name: order_payments_raw_27
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  payment_type
FROM olist_order_payments
WHERE payment_type IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per payment record (order_id + payment_sequential)
views.description: Cleaned/normalized payment records for each order. Exposes order_id and payment_type and a single raw payment record row per olist_order_payments row (each counted once). Filters out NULL payment_type.

views.name: orders_cohort_delivered
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_approved_at,
  o.order_delivered_customer_date
FROM orders_base o
WHERE o.order_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Cohort of valid orders to consider: exposes orders present in the orders table with key timestamps and status. Intended to be joined to order items and payments to ensure only existing/valid orders are counted.

views.name: order_payments_raw_29
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  payment_sequential,
  payment_type,
  payment_value
FROM olist_order_payments
views.description: Raw payment rows for orders. Keeps each payment row (payment_sequential) as its own record with payment type and value, for counting or summing. No filtering by order status.

views.name: category_payment_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.order_id,
  p.payment_sequential,
  p.payment_type,
  p.payment_value,
  pc.product_category_name
FROM
  olist_order_payments AS p
JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    oi.order_id,
    oi.product_id,
    pd.product_category_name
  FROM
    olist_order_items AS oi
  JOIN
    olist_products AS pd
    ON oi.product_id = pd.product_id
) AS pc
  ON p.order_id = pc.order_id
views.description: Denormalized payment event rows annotated with the product category(ies) present in the corresponding order. Produces one row per payment row x product category present in that order to enable counting payments per category. (If an order contains items from multiple categories, the payment event will appear once for each category present.)

views.name: geolocation_clean
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  CAST(geolocation_lat AS REAL) AS geolocation_lat,
  CAST(geolocation_lng AS REAL) AS geolocation_lng,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_state
FROM olist_geolocation
WHERE geolocation_lat IS NOT NULL
  AND geolocation_lng IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng, geolocation_city, geolocation_state
views.description: Normalized/cleaned geolocation rows with non-null coordinates and canonical zip prefix, exposing location keys and lat/lng as numeric for geospatial calculations.

views.name: geolocation_ordered_with_prev
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  LAG(geolocation_state) OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS state_prev,
  LAG(geolocation_city) OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS city_prev,
  LAG(geolocation_zip_code_prefix) OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_zip_code_prefix_prev,
  LAG(geolocation_lat) OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS lat_prev,
  LAG(geolocation_lng) OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS lng_prev,
  geolocation_state,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  geolocation_lat,
  geolocation_lng,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY geolocation_state, geolocation_city, geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng) AS row_order_index
FROM geolocation_clean
WHERE geolocation_lat IS NOT NULL
  AND geolocation_lng IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per geolocation row augmented with its immediate predecessor (LAG) in the specified ordering
views.description: Geolocation rows ordered by state, city, zip_prefix, lat, lng with LEAD/LAG to return the immediate predecessor or successor rows for each row to support consecutive-row distance calculations.
